abstract: This lecture reviews abnormal uterine bleeding, focusing on physiologic dysfunctional uterine bleeding. It covers normal menstrual cycle parameters, definitions of abnormal bleeding patterns, and the hormonal regulation of the menstrual cycle. The speaker discusses clinical scenarios including menarche, perimenopause, and polycystic ovary syndrome, emphasizing history-taking and treatment strategies.
key_points: Normal menstrual interval is 21-35 days, duration 5-7 days.
Quantify bleeding by asking number of pads/tampons used on the heaviest day.
When taking a bleeding history, establish the patient's normal cycle off birth control.
After menarche, allow up to 2 years for cycles to regulate before evaluating for chronic anovulation.
Perimenopause onset is defined by irregular periods, not hot flashes; mean age 45, duration 2-8 years.
In PCOS, high testosterone reduces SHBG; treatment with high-estrogen birth control pills increases SHBG and reduces hirsutism.
A rapid rise in estrogen triggers an LH surge, which triggers ovulation.
Progesterone withdrawal causes menstruation; exogenous progestin withdrawal can also induce bleeding.
Women over 60 with any bleeding should be evaluated for endometrial cancer.
Combined oral contraceptives treat both dysmenorrhea and perimenopausal irregular bleeding by thinning the endometrium.
